cards.text: The LORD gives the prophet Jeremiah a message for Judah and Jerusalem, and it opens with an order: “Blow the ram’s horn throughout the land.” Friend, that is NOT a snooze button alarm. Nobody gets nine more minutes on this one.

cards.question: The ram’s horn is blowing across Judah. What does the cry tell the people to do?

answers.text: March out and face the army
Gather at the temple to pray

cards.text: Raise a signal flag toward Zion, the message says, and “Seek refuge! Do not delay!” Not after one more episode, friend. NOW.

cards.question: The LORD says this disaster is coming, but He has nothing to do with it.
The LORD tells Judah He is bringing disaster from the ___, and terrible destruction.

cards.text: Then the LORD paints the picture: “A lion has gone up from his thicket, and a destroyer of nations has set out.” In my junk drawer days, the scariest thing that ever came out of hiding was a dust bunny, and this is a LION.

cards.question: The lion has left his lair. What has he set out to do to Judah’s land?

answers.text: Pass it by on his way

cards.question: Judah’s cities will be ruins with no one living in them, and the fierce anger of the LORD has not turned away. So what are the people told to do?

answers.text: Put on fine robes and celebrate

cards.text: In that day, the LORD says, the king and officials will lose their courage, and the priests will tremble in fear. Then Jeremiah cries out, “Ah, Lord GOD, how completely You have deceived this people and Jerusalem” and says a sword is at their throats.

cards.question: Jeremiah says the people were told, You will have ___, while a sword is at their throats.

cards.text: Then comes word of a searing wind from the barren heights in the desert, blowing toward His people. The LORD says this wind comes from Him.

cards.question: This searing wind is the gentle kind, the kind used to winnow and sift.

cards.text: “Behold, he advances like the clouds, his chariots like the whirlwind.” This army doesn’t show up, friend. It ARRIVES.

cards.question: The invader is moving fast. His horses are swifter than ___.

cards.text: Then comes the cry, “Woe to us, for we are ruined!” But right in the middle of the alarm, Jerusalem hears a call.

cards.question: In the middle of the alarm, Jerusalem is told to wash something away so she may be saved. What is it?

cards.text: Then a voice resounds from Dan, proclaiming disaster from the hills of Ephraim, moving faster than a rumor in the office group chat. The news: a besieging army is coming from a distant land, raising their voices against the cities of Judah.

cards.question: The army surrounds Judah like men guarding a field. Why does the LORD say this is happening?

answers.text: Her walls were built too weak

cards.question: The LORD tells Judah that her own ways and deeds have brought this on her.

cards.text: Then the prophet cries out, “My anguish, my anguish! I writhe in pain!” His heart pounds within him, and he says he cannot be silent.

cards.question: The prophet’s heart is pounding and he can’t stay quiet. What has he heard?

answers.text: The horn and the alarm of battle
A voice calling out his name

cards.text: Disaster after disaster is proclaimed, and the whole land is laid waste. The prophet says even his own tents and curtains are destroyed.

cards.question: The prophet’s tents and curtains are destroyed. How fast does he say it happened?

cards.text: He asks, “How long must I see the signal flag and hear the sound of the horn?” He’s been hearing that horn since the very first line, and then the LORD speaks about His people.

cards.question: The LORD says His people are foolish children without understanding. They are skilled in doing ___, but they know not how to do ___.

cards.text: Then the prophet says, “I looked at the earth, and it was formless and void; I looked to the heavens, and they had no light.” “Formless and void” is how Genesis 1:2 describes the earth at the very beginning.

cards.question: In the prophet’s vision, he looks at the mountains and the hills. What are they doing?
When the prophet looks again in his vision, the land is still full of people.
In the vision, all the cities are torn down before the LORD’s fierce anger, and the fruitful land has become a ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks: “The whole land will be desolate,” and He doesn’t stop there. There’s one more line.

cards.question: The LORD says He will finish the land’s destruction completely.
The earth will mourn and the heavens will grow dark. The LORD says He has spoken and He has planned. Will He change course?

answers.text: No He will not turn back
Yes if the people beg Him

cards.text: At the sound of the horseman and archer, every city flees. People run into the thickets and climb among the rocks.

cards.question: Once the people flee, every city is abandoned, with no one left living there.

cards.text: Then the message turns to someone called “O devastated one.” She dresses herself in scarlet, puts on gold jewelry and paints her eyes.

cards.question: The devastated one dresses up in scarlet and gold. What do her lovers think of her?

cards.text: Then the prophet hears a cry like a woman in labor with her first child. It’s the Daughter of Zion, gasping for breath and stretching out her hands.

cards.question: The Daughter of Zion cries, Woe is me, for my soul faints before the ___.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 7 quotes "Formless and void", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 16 quotes "O devastated one.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card says the LORD speaks Jeremiah 4:7 ("Then the LORD paints the picture"). The text doesn't say who speaks this verse. The quote it sits in ends in 4:8 with "the fierce anger of the LORD has not turned away from us," which refers to the LORD in the third person and includes the speaker in "us." Assigning the lion picture to the LORD closes something the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the next word of the line "His horses are swifter than ___." Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason out eagles over leopards or gazelles. It tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The question says the army surrounds Judah. In Jeremiah 4:16-17, "They surround her" follows "Proclaim to Jerusalem," so "her" could be Jerusalem. The card picks Judah where the text leaves it open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card says "He's been hearing that horn since the very first line." Jeremiah 4:5 only commands that the horn be blown. The first time the prophet says he hears it is 4:19. What the card points out isn't true to the text.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The card states as fact that she dresses in scarlet, puts on gold jewelry and paints her eyes. In Jeremiah 4:30 each of these comes after "though" ("what will you do, though you dress yourself in scarlet, though you adorn yourself with gold jewelry, though you enlarge your eyes with paint?"). The card drops the "though."
The question says "The devastated one dresses up in scarlet and gold" as a fact. In Jeremiah 4:30 this comes after "though."

The blank asks the baker to guess the last word of the Daughter of Zion's line ("murderers"). The earlier cards never told the setup that would let a baker reason it out, which is that her lovers "want to take your life" (4:30). Priests and prophets are just as easy to pick, so the right answer comes down to luck.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
